questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The ranking of Imperial College London is really high and I was wondering how is it possible and why.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information was very limited. We got emails very late upon arrival but most of the things was received very last minutes (which we found out was the style of doing it in London).  I needed to keep emailing to my coordinator in London serveral times in different ways before receciving an answer

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We recieved information about accomodation, transport in London and so on

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Really hard, specially because I was only going to stay there for 4 months. Short term lent is very hard to find and very expensive. Recommendation is probably using "shareroom", "zoopla" but very hard to find serious ones not scam or other thing. But also ask the people you meet there and in Whatsapp group for Erasmus(ESN) do not hesitate but just ask in the group. I arrived without a long term accomodation and found very expensive one in London by property company(rr property) but you can definitely find cheaper and better ones.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You will not be offered accommodation from Imperial if you are staying only for one term(at least this year 21/22). but the halls(campus accommodation can be placed very far, so be careful with it) but price should be very good. When u live off campus which I did, remember to keep on with the socials. There are numberous people want to meet up and do stuff and it makes the experience soooo much better.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is not that complicated, but need efforts

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were pretty difficult. But good news is at exams you will have to choose 4 out of 8 questions to answer or 3 out of 6(only examples, but more or less like this).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very little lab work, a lot of lectures and a lot of self-study  - very different from UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Structure Biology and Drug Design

Integrative Systems Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I may not recommend these courses, it is very different from what we had in UCPH. But would like to give a description 

Structure Biology and Drug Design had many lectures in methods in Structure Biology; Cryo-EM, X-ray crystallography, NMR and X-file. it was a lot of Physics about how the machinery works - Amplitude, waves and so on. There were 2-4 lectures about Drug design which were very interesting. Coursework for the course was modelling in program coot with x-ray data and NMR assignment in ccpnmr.  For me, I never heard of those programmes and it was hard to do it when u need to find out how by yourself. 

Integrative Systems Biology; modelling biology with math model -  A lot of math - I was really a fan of the first math course in CPH but found out that I forgot almost everything. It is a more complicated version of math. We had about e.g. dynamic system and bayesian interference. If you are a big fan of those and love programming in python and Matlab choose these courses. 

To summarise, I chose courses that I had never heard of in UCPH and thought that it was a good opportunity to have them. But they were a lot harder than I thought. This is because the students there may already have the fundamentals for these 3rd-year courses but I didn't. They were indeed interesting, but I definitely struggled. If you want more time to do socials and culture stuff, select modules that you are more confident in :)

How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were so many societies - like sports clubs(rowing, badminton, football, hockey...) you can find everything, choir, acapella, reading society, culture (different countries and languages). Academic societies as well. 
There were more than 200 societies/clubs at the University.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You have to join the ESN imperial - for all the Erasmus student at Imperial and if you want to do anything there is an opportunity (information on imperial student unions website).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You have to see London, but as well go somewhere else than London. For example Cambrigde, Oxford, Edinburgh...

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Imperial is so international or London is so international. By meeting with those Imperial students and the Erasmus ones. You will almost feel at home when exploring so much stuff. There are various thing you can do in London you will never feel bored.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to lectures and just talk to somebody, tell them you are exchanging and want tips on where to eat or where to go and socialize with local students. Most of them are open and welcoming

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really but always have sorry and please in the sentence, it never hurts.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warm people. I think because you are not from London people are even nicer to you. I've heard that people are not that nice in London, which is not so true for my personal experience

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be positive, open and bold

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The information may be limited and the process will be time-consuming, complicated and really need effort. But believe me that it is worth it. If you can go on exchange for 2 semesters do it!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I would say that I was very active and did loads of stuff. I may have met some friends for life and everyone who I've met either had done exchange or doing exchange right now only said you have to go on exchange. The most rewarding part is the people you meet, they are all very different and interesting compared to your study here in Copenahgen. They have a lot of experience and may be very international and you learn so much from them already. Not to mention that you will study in a very prestige University and gain knowledge about the UK

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge can be a lot of things. But leaving was the hardest. A lot of my friends will stay there for a year and I was not finished either - in the manner that there is still a lot of things that I haven't done yet. It says a lot how amazing it has been since the greatest challenge was leaving.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
